Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data patterns:

## Example 1 (2025-06-05)
- History: Price started around 70.91-73.41 range, showing some volatility
- Sentiment: Mix of values from 0.00 to 1.00
- Model forecasts: Around 72.64-76.82 range initially, then 70.90-75.77
- True outcomes: 72.74, 73.50, 74.23, 72.66, 74.36, 75.39, 75.94, 75.34, 74.64, 74.61, 72.74, 72.97, 73.27, 73.54, 71.15, 70.40, 70.96, 68.97, 70.58, 71.93, 72.06, 71.67, 71.20, 70.42, 70.39, 70.74, 70.55, 70.42, 71.51, 71.31

Looking at the discrepancies:
- At day 1: Model 72.64 vs True 72.74 (off by -0.10)
- At day 5: Model 74.74 vs True 74.36 (off by +0.38)
- At day 9: Model 75.71 vs True 74.61 (off by +1.10)
- At day 18: Model 70.90 vs True 68.97 (off by +1.93)
- At day 20: Model 74.24 vs True 71.93 (off by +2.31)

The model seems to be consistently forecasting prices that are too HIGH, especially as we get further into the 30-day horizon. The true outcomes appear to be trending DOWNWARD and LOWER than the model forecasts.


I notice a clear divergence pattern where the model overestimates prices, particularly as time progresses. The forecasts consistently hover above true values, with the gap widening between days 18-20. Sentiment seems to play a complex role, not providing a straightforward correction mechanism.
